one_line: Young Afghan jagirdar and future ruler, serving as a landholder’s son and revenue manager in north India.

appearance.age_look: Mid-20s to early-30s, lean but wiry build, athletic and used to riding and outdoor work.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, sharp jawline and neatly trimmed short beard and moustache; medium-brown north Indian-Afghan complexion with sun-browned cheeks; thick arched brows and intense, observant eyes; default expression calm, focused and slightly stern, as if constantly assessing.
appearance.hair: Thick, dark brown-black hair kept relatively short and tidy, barely visible under a soft round Afghan-style cap (kulah) made of dark indigo cloth with a narrow band of muted gold embroidery around the edge.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, knee-length Afghan-Indian robe (angarkha) of matte dusty-olive cotton, overlapping and tying slightly off-center at the chest with simple cloth ties, worn over a cream-colored, high-necked cotton tunic; a narrow, dark maroon leather belt wraps the waist, holding a small pouch; loose, straight churidar-style trousers in pale beige taper cleanly at the ankles; on his feet are sturdy brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes, practical for riding and walking; over one shoulder he drapes a lightweight plain-weave shawl in muted slate-blue, sometimes pulled around him in cooler weather; no ornate royal jewelry, just a simple silver ring and a modest cord bracelet, emphasizing a serious, working landholder rather than a courtier.
appearance.signature: A single, slightly curved Indo-Afghan talwar with a plain steel blade, simple iron cross-guard, and a dark brown leather-wrapped hilt, worn sheathed at his left hip in an unornamented brown scabbard, symbolizing both personal defense and disciplined authority.

ref_desc: Young Farid Khan has a medium-brown oval face with a neat short beard, dark eyes and a calm stern gaze, dark hair under an indigo Afghan cap, wearing a dusty-olive angarkha over cream tunic and beige churidar with brown shoes and slate-blue shawl, carrying a plain-hilted talwar at his left hip in a brown scabbard with accents of muted maroon and brown leather.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of young Farid Khan (later Sher Shah) as a dignified early-16th-century Afghan jagirdar: a lean, athletic man in his late twenties with a medium-brown north Indian-Afghan complexion, oval face, straight nose, sharp jawline, thick brows and intense, observant dark eyes, his expression calm, focused and slightly stern; he has thick dark brown-black hair kept short and mostly hidden under a soft round indigo Afghan-style cloth cap with a narrow band of muted gold embroidery; he wears a matte dusty-olive cotton angarkha, knee-length, overlapping and tied slightly off-center at the chest over a cream high-necked cotton tunic, belted at the waist with a narrow dark maroon leather belt holding a small pouch; his loose pale beige churidar trousers taper at the ankles into sturdy brown leather shoes with slightly upturned toes; a lightweight muted slate-blue shawl is draped over one shoulder; there is no royal finery, only a simple silver ring and modest cord bracelet; at his left hip hangs his signature weapon, a plain Indo-Afghan talwar with a slightly curved steel blade, simple iron cross-guard, dark brown leather-wrapped hilt and unornamented brown scabbard; show him from multiple angles to emphasize the consistent dusty-olive, cream, muted maroon, slate-blue and brown leather palette and the practical, historically grounded early-1500s north Indian-Afghan costume.
